dayToDay.notes: Students are with their guide group essentially the entire trip, sleeping outdoors at shared backcountry campsites, with a staff-to-camper ratio of at least 2 staff per 10 youth. Days are highly structured: hiking, a daily morning meeting, evening group activities and a campfire, and shared meals prepared together. There's no cell service in the backcountry, so there's no phone or text contact with family during the trip — guides send a nightly satellite check-in to the office, not to parents, consistent with the program's "no news is good news" approach. Parents receive a recap email with photos and a daily journal about 1–2 weeks after the trip ends.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Lasting Adventures Yosemite summer camp FAQ pages (identical language across 6-Day Young Adventurer's, 6-Day High Country, and 10-Day Mammoth pages)

dayToDay.notes: This is an island-based residential camp with structured cabin groups of about 8-10 campers per counselor; certified dive staff supervise at closer ratios (1 instructor per 4 campers for scuba certification, 1 per 8 for snorkeling). There is no phone contact between parents and campers at all during a session - the camp states this is an intentional independence policy, not just a logistics limitation. The only outbound communication is one-way: parents get 5 free email credits per camper per week (more purchasable), and campers can write letters, but there's no video call or phone option. In-session visits or tours from parents are not permitted. A registered nurse is on-site for the full summer.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Catalina Sea Camp 1-Week Programs page and Parent FAQs

dayToDay.notes: This is a highly structured, academically intensive residential program: the daily schedule runs from 7am breakfast to 10pm, with classes and research in the morning, problem sessions or additional classes in the afternoon, and study groups in the evening. Campers are explicitly not permitted to take online courses or participate in any other program, in person or online, during the six weeks - an unusually strict exclusivity policy compared to most residential camps. Parent visits during camp are allowed but require prior approval through a request form, rather than being either fully open or fully prohibited.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Mathworks HSMC program page and Camps visit-request page (txst.edu/mathworks)
